IV. 3. 5.] UPARIPAÑCA-VAGGA 3. 127

19. Then Ragâ, the daughter of Mâra, spoke this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
Having severed the craving, the crowd, and the current,
Truly many beings will pass over.
Indeed, this homeless one
Will sever and carry away the multitude to the King of Death.

20. The great heroes, the Tathâgatas,
Lead by the true doctrine.
Of those being led by the doctrine,
What envy can the wise have?

21. Then Taṇhâ, Arati, and Ragâ, the daughters of Mâra, approached Mâra the Evil One.

22. Mâra the Evil One saw Taṇhâ, Arati, and Ragâ, the daughters of Mâra, coming from afar. Seeing them, he spoke in verses:
Fools, you crush a mountain with lotus stalks,
You dig a mountain with your fingernails,
You bite iron with your teeth.
Striking your head against a rock,
You seek footing in the abyss.
Like crashing your chest against a post,
You return disheartened from Gotama.

23. Shaking with agitation, Taṇhâ, Arati, and Ragâ came.
The Teacher dispelled them there,
As the wind blows away a heap of cotton.

->The Third Chapter<-
->Summary of this chapter<-
Sambahula, Samiddhi, Godhika, the Seven Years,
The daughters, taught by the Buddha-teacher, this is the Mâra Group of Five.
The Connected Discourses on Mâra is concluded.

<summary>This page recounts the unsuccessful attempts of Mâra's daughters to distract the Buddha, culminating in their retreat and a concluding summary of the Mâra section.</summary>
